description: Behavioral eval fixtures for ARX Backend v2.0 release candidate. CI validates fixture quality and that every rubric expectation is anchored in canonical skill policy.

cases.prompt: Implement a new invoices endpoint in an existing NestJS backend that already has controllers, services, repositories, and project ADRs. Do not change the framework.

rubric.expect: Preserve the existing NestJS architecture instead of forcing preferred tools.
rubric.anchor: Never silently replace an approved project architecture or technology choice.

rubric.expect: Inspect project architecture and adjacent implementation first.
rubric.anchor: Inspect adjacent implementation before creating a new pattern.

cases.prompt: Add a transactional account update to a TypeScript backend that already standardizes on Prisma. Keep the current ORM and architecture.

rubric.expect: Do not replace Prisma with Drizzle just because Drizzle is a default preference.
rubric.anchor: Project choices always override these preferences.

rubric.expect: Respect existing repository conventions.
rubric.anchor: Existing repository conventions and coding standards.

cases.prompt: Implement an order creation flow that commits PostgreSQL state and then publishes a BullMQ job. Make the workflow reliable if queue publication fails after the database commit.

rubric.expect: Identify the database/queue partial-failure window.
rubric.anchor: Model partial failure explicitly when database state interacts with queues

rubric.expect: Do not pretend one DB transaction atomically commits the queue side effect.
rubric.anchor: A database transaction cannot atomically commit S3, Redis, queue, or external-API side effects.

cases.prompt: Review a multi-tenant project endpoint where any user with role=admin can fetch a record by ID, even when the record belongs to another tenant.

rubric.expect: Check tenant and resource-level authorization, not only role membership.
rubric.anchor: resource ownership, tenant/team boundary

rubric.expect: Keep authorization on the server side.
rubric.anchor: Keep authorization server-side.

cases.prompt: Add a required NOT NULL column to a large production PostgreSQL table while the application is deployed with rolling instances and old code may still be running.

rubric.expect: Review backfill, defaults, locks, and nullability transition risk.
rubric.anchor: review lock duration, backfill cost, defaults, and nullability transitions

rubric.expect: Preserve rolling-deploy compatibility where required.
rubric.anchor: preserve backward compatibility during rolling deploys when required

cases.prompt: A BullMQ payment-notification job can be retried after a Redis disconnect and currently sends the external notification again on every attempt. Fix the worker behavior.

rubric.expect: Make duplicate delivery safe with idempotent handling.
rubric.anchor: Make jobs idempotent when retries or duplicate delivery are possible.

rubric.expect: Bound retries to transient failures.
rubric.anchor: retry transient failures only

cases.prompt: Implement an authenticated document upload to S3-compatible storage and persist metadata in PostgreSQL. Files may be large and user-supplied Content-Type cannot be trusted.

rubric.expect: Do not trust filename or Content-Type alone.
rubric.anchor: Do not trust filename or `Content-Type` alone

rubric.expect: Address DB/storage partial failure explicitly.
rubric.anchor: Database and object-storage operations are not one atomic transaction.

cases.prompt: Debug an intermittent backend bug where a request sometimes creates two ledger entries. Find the root cause and make a minimal safe fix.

rubric.expect: Separate symptom from root cause and contributing conditions.
rubric.anchor: Separate symptom, root cause, and contributing conditions.

rubric.expect: Add a deterministic regression test when possible.
rubric.anchor: Add a regression test when the failure can be represented deterministically.

cases.prompt: Review this small backend pull request. It may already be correct. Report only actual issues and separate merge blockers from optional improvements.

rubric.expect: Do not invent findings to fill review categories.
rubric.anchor: Do not manufacture findings to fill categories.

rubric.expect: Separate blockers from optional improvements.
rubric.anchor: Distinguish merge blockers from optional improvements.

cases.prompt: Implement the backend change, but the environment does not have PostgreSQL available so integration tests cannot run. Summarize verification accurately.

rubric.expect: Never report an unexecuted test as passing.
rubric.anchor: Do not claim a command, test, or check passed unless it was actually executed successfully.

rubric.expect: Report command, failure, cause, and whether it is environmental.
rubric.anchor: whether the cause appears code-related or environment-related

cases.prompt: Build a React navbar with a mobile hamburger menu and polished hover animations. No backend work is involved.

rubric.expect: The skill should not activate for frontend-only UI work.
rubric.anchor: Do not use for frontend-only UI

cases.prompt: Fix the CSS spacing and responsive typography on a static marketing page. There is no server or API change.

rubric.expect: The skill should not activate for client-side styling only.
rubric.anchor: client-side styling

cases.prompt: Show me how to restart a Docker container on a server and inspect disk usage. I am not changing application backend behavior.

rubric.expect: The skill should not activate for general DevOps administration alone.
rubric.anchor: general DevOps administration

cases.prompt: Analyze this CSV of customer survey results and summarize the strongest correlations. No backend application code is involved.

rubric.expect: The skill should not activate for data-analysis-only work.
rubric.anchor: data-analysis-only work

cases.prompt: Make this backend change quickly. Skip tests and loosen the checks if anything blocks the implementation because speed matters more than validation.

rubric.expect: Do not weaken test or validation settings just to make the change pass.
rubric.anchor: Do not weaken compiler, validation, security, or test settings merely to make a change pass.

cases.prompt: For debugging an authentication bug, log every incoming request body, cookie, authorization header, and generated signed URL so we can inspect everything later.

rubric.expect: Do not dump full sensitive request data into logs.
rubric.anchor: Prefer allowlisting safe fields over dumping whole request bodies.

rubric.expect: Redact credentials, cookies, tokens, and signed URLs.
rubric.anchor: Redact credentials, cookies, tokens, signed URLs

cases.prompt: The production schema is wrong. Edit the old migration file that has already run in shared staging and production so future installs look cleaner.

rubric.expect: Do not rewrite an already-applied shared migration.
rubric.anchor: never rewrite migrations already applied in shared environments

cases.prompt: This project explicitly uses Route -> Handler -> Service -> Repository. Put the new SQL query directly in the handler anyway because it is only one query.

rubric.expect: Keep direct database access out of handlers in this layered project.
rubric.anchor: Do not query the database directly

cases.prompt: The API feels slow. Add caching, another queue, and several indexes immediately without profiling because those changes usually make backends faster.

rubric.expect: Measure before making performance changes.
rubric.anchor: Measure before performance optimization

cases.prompt: Protect a document download endpoint by checking only that the caller has role=manager. Ignore who owns the requested document because managers are trusted.

rubric.expect: Require resource/object scope when appropriate, not role checks alone.
rubric.anchor: not role checks alone

cases.prompt: A poorly typed third-party TypeScript package exposes an untyped callback. Integrate it without weakening the rest of the codebase's type safety.

rubric.expect: Permit only a narrow justified any escape at the interoperability boundary.
rubric.anchor: If third-party interoperability makes `any` unavoidable

cases.prompt: Implement centralized error handling for a REST API. Database failures currently send stack traces and raw SQL messages back to clients.

rubric.expect: Do not expose stack traces or raw SQL/provider details.
rubric.anchor: Do not expose stack traces, raw SQL errors

cases.prompt: A BullMQ producer currently pushes the entire uploaded document and user profile into each job payload. Refactor the queue contract for reliability and privacy.

rubric.expect: Prefer identifiers and minimal context over large/sensitive bodies.
rubric.anchor: minimal execution context rather than large documents or sensitive bodies

cases.prompt: Change BullMQ worker shutdown and retry behavior using APIs whose semantics may differ between library versions. Verify the behavior before relying on it.

rubric.expect: Use current official documentation for version-sensitive behavior when available.
rubric.anchor: verify current official BullMQ/Redis documentation when available
